title: This Isn’t Your Typical Chinese Carbon Bike | Incolor SR+ Build

takeaways.text: The painted 58 cm SR+ frame weighed 920 g with its hardware. Incolor quotes 720 g unpainted without hardware; the builders found the gap plausible for a large painted frame.

The Di2 battery sits in a carrier inside the frame above the bottom bracket, so the very thin seatpost can be removed without unplugging it. Hose and wire routing through the frame was rated about 6/10 for difficulty.

Incolor's Aero Win one-piece bar (140 mm stem here, lengths to 150 mm) has very low stack and a negative stem angle with a cable spacer underneath. The hosts called it heavy at about 400 g but stiff, and its routing about 7/10 for difficulty.

On this 2× build the fitted GP5000 tires measured about 32.5 mm with little room left. The mechanics doubted 38 mm tires would fit and expected even 35 mm to be tight on a wide rim. Incolor rates 38 mm for 1× builds only and 32 mm for 2×; no larger tire was test-fitted.
The supplied Incolor aero bottles sit low on the frame by design; the hosts found them rattly, hard to grab and awkward to refill, though aerodynamic.
The very light seatpost uses a 3D-printed titanium clamp head; the builders questioned how robust its thin sections are over potholes but did not test it.
Verdict from the bench: good finish, tidy routing and a stiff bar, but buyers must accept the curved offset steerer and an aggressive geometry that may not suit very tall riders.

disclosure: Published by Crafted Cycles, a custom-build workshop promoting its services in the description; this is shop-produced build context.
summary: Workshop build of the Incolor Speedster SR+ with a custom component selection. It shows the SR+ version, not the SSR or a factory complete-bike configuration for the SR.
